skill.name: near-smart-contracts
skill.description: NEAR Protocol smart contract development guidance for Rust, near-sdk v5, cross-contract calls, testing, storage, migrations, and security patterns.
skill.summary: Guide Rust NEAR smart contract design, review, testing, deployment, and security patterns.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, Rust NEAR environment APIs, documentation links, and test-only keys. The remote installer commands in SKILL.md use pipe-to-shell patterns, which are a real critical risk if an agent executes them automatically. No prompt injection or hidden data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell commands with safer install steps that download installers, verify checksums or signatures, and require explicit user confirmation before execution.
Pin installer versions or releases where possible, and link to official verification instructions for Rust, cargo-near, and near-cli-rs.

remediation.issue: Sensitive key examples need stronger boundaries
remediation.suggestion: Label private key examples as off-chain only, recommend dedicated test keys, and warn users not to expose production signer credentials to agents.

content.value_statement: NEAR contract development requires precise Rust patterns for storage, calls, migrations, testing, and security. This skill gives Codex, Claude, and Claude Code practical NEAR SDK guidance for building and reviewing contracts.
actual_capabilities: Explains NEAR SDK v5 contract structure, initialization, serializers, and PanicOnDefault usage.
Shows secure storage payment checks, refunds, access control, and small deposit protections.
Guides cross-contract promises, private callbacks, gas allocation, callback results, and yield/resume workflows.
Documents state migration, upgrade patterns, and versioned state planning for deployed contracts.
Covers integration testing with near-sandbox, near-api, gas checks, and failure scenarios.
Summarizes chain signatures and multichain transaction signing patterns with MPC callbacks.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not compile, deploy, or audit contracts by itself.
Tool version references may need verification against current NEAR releases before production use.
Examples require adaptation for each contract, account model, and governance process.
It does not replace formal smart contract security review or mainnet launch checks.

use_cases.title: Create a NEAR contract
use_cases.description: A developer uses the skill to structure contracts, choose SDK macros, and add storage checks before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review cross-contract behavior
use_cases.description: An engineer checks promise chaining, callbacks, gas allocation, and migration plans before deploying an update.

use_cases.title: Plan integration tests
use_cases.description: A tester designs near-sandbox scenarios for deployment, calls, balances, callbacks, failures, and time-sensitive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a contract outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new NEAR contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the near-smart-contracts skill to outline a Rust NEAR contract for [purpose]. Include state, initialization, storage checks, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review storage safety
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused security review of a payable write flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the near-smart-contracts skill to review this storage update flow: [describe flow]. Identify missing deposits, refunds, and access checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design cross-contract calls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the near-smart-contracts skill to design a promise chain between [contract A] and [contract B]. Include gas, callbacks, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan migration and signing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced upgrade and chain signatures design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the near-smart-contracts skill to plan a migration from [old state] to [new state], then add MPC signing for [target chain].

output_examples.input: Review a payable method that writes user data.
output: Compute storage usage before and after the write.
Require enough attached deposit and refund extra NEAR.
Test low-deposit and unauthorized caller cases.

output_examples.input: Plan a contract upgrade with a new state field.
output: Define the old state shape before deployment.
Add a private migration entry point for the new state.
Deploy code and call migration in one controlled flow.
Use governance or multisig approval for production updates.

output_examples.input: Design an MPC signing flow for Ethereum.
output: Derive the foreign address before funding it.
Build the unsigned transaction off-chain or in contract logic.
Request the MPC signature with enough gas and a callback.
Finalize and broadcast the signed transaction off-chain.

best_practices: Use cargo-near templates, then verify generated settings before adding business logic.
Update state only after promise results are checked in private callbacks.
Treat private keys and signer credentials as off-chain secrets with explicit handling rules.
anti_patterns: Piping remote installers directly into a shell without verification.
Deploying changed state layouts without a migration method and rollback plan.
Using unprotected resume or callback methods for external data.

faq.question: Does this skill write code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and examples. The user or agent still chooses edits and runs checks.

faq.question: Which NEAR SDK version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets near-sdk-rs v5.x patterns, including the newer near macro syntax.

faq.question: Can it help with security review?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights common NEAR risks, but it does not replace independent security review.

faq.question: Does it support chain signatures?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains MPC signing flows, payload construction, callbacks, and off-chain transaction finalization.

faq.question: Can it deploy to mainnet?
faq.answer: No. It documents deployment commands, but account choice, signing, and network actions require user control.

faq.question: Why is installation guidance flagged?
faq.answer: The skill includes pipe-to-shell installer examples. Marketplace users should verify installers before running them.
